scope_definition: Core MHA/GQA attention framework APIs: holistic BatchAttention, single prefill/decode, paged batch prefill/decode, ragged batch prefill, and their documented lifecycle surface. CUDA/TRT-LLM-specific adapters, MLA, sparse attention, cascade, POD, and page mutation APIs are outside this phase.

entries.notes: Public plan/run facade executes mixed paged prefill/decode requests and always returns output plus LSE. device='cpu' is an explicit oracle opt-in; an NPU device owns a private mode-bound provider resolver.

Package-backed runs validate Q and unquantized packed/separate KV metadata against the active plan before provider lowering. Quantized KV stays on its exact QuantSpec and physical-layout path; physical storage, scale, zero-point and dynamic per-head scale tensor views participate in provider alignment and output/input alias validation.

Exact snapshot signature with executable Host ReferenceTensor semantics. backend='reference' explicitly selects the oracle; backend='auto' with NPU tensors owns an ephemeral provider resolver. Explicit quantized K/V logical shapes drive the plan. Bare FP8 Q/K/V canonicalize into the same internal QuantSpec route without exposing a plan wrapper; omitted per-head scales use virtual unit semantics only when the provider binding certifies argument omission as scale=1. Per-head scale_q/scale_k/scale_v and calibration k_scale/v_scale remain distinct sources and each requires an exact provider argument binding. NVFP4 kv_cache_sf has a provider-independent metadata contract, a plan-bound packed-storage/scale joint view, a joint lowering adapter, and an auditable runtime-spec route tied to one exact packed QuantSpec/layout/argument binding; production provider contribution and execution remain explicit gaps.

Host injected-module protocol freezes the upstream signature, 32 MiB scratch metadata, output/LSE shapes, NHD/HND and mask codes, and exact run argument order. It does not compile, load, or authenticate an Ascend JIT artifact.

The public wrapper keeps backend='reference' as an explicit Host oracle and routes backend='auto' with an NPU workspace through a private, mode-bound provider runtime. No provider is enabled by default; unbound provider options fail before package invocation. An FP8 kv_data_type becomes the canonical per-tensor provider QuantSpec; separate bare K/V use authorized virtual scalar unit scales, while combined provider storage remains fail-closed.

Exact snapshot signature. Host reference reports (0, 0). Provider queries use an unpublished runtime fork over the wrapper's frozen registry and return the selected operation's caller-workspace requirement without mutating active plan state; package-managed workspace currently reports (0, 0).
For an NPU provider plan, an FP8 kv_data_type is normalized into the canonical per-tensor QuantSpec before selection; the Host oracle continues to read logical FP8 ReferenceTensor inputs directly.

The public signature includes current upstream q/k/v scales, caller-owned buffers, runtime window, attention sinks, NVFP4 scale factors, skip-softmax sparsity, FP16 softmax, and SP-compression controls. The Host oracle rejects enabled backend-specific features that it cannot represent. Provider q_scale/k_scale/v_scale remain independent dynamic sources on the reusable plan and each accepts a finite scalar or an exact per-head tensor; provider bootstrap must cover both forms. Per-head scale tensors obey provider alignment and output alias rules. Unquantized packed/separate KV is metadata-validated for layout, shape, page capacity, dtype, device, access policy and aliases before lowering. Quantized storage/scale/zero-point views also participate in alignment and output alias checks. Caller-owned out/lse require exact mutable buffer arguments in the operation catalog and otherwise fail closed. Bare separate FP8 K/V are canonicalized internally only under exact implicit-unit authorization.
Backend-neutral name avoids exposing CUDA terminology; fixed-shape semantics are preserved.

Public wrapper covers ragged request segmentation, GQA, NHD/HND, masks, scalar Q/K/V scale, scalar output-scale and LSE semantics. Host reference is explicit; an NPU workspace owns a private mode-bound provider resolver. Provider scale forwarding requires exact scalar input-kind declarations; output-scale also requires an eligible planned output dtype.
Caller-owned out/lse are admitted only when the selected operation catalog declares distinct mutable buffer arguments; metadata, writability, access policy, and aliases are validated before lowering.

Exact snapshot signature with executable Host ReferenceTensor semantics. ReferenceTensor inputs explicitly opt into the oracle because the upstream API has no backend argument; NPU tensors own an ephemeral provider resolver. Explicit quantized K/V logical shapes drive the plan. Bare matching FP8 Q/K/V canonicalize to an internal per-tensor QuantSpec whose virtual scalar K/V unit scales may be omitted only under an exact provider declaration. q_scale and k_scale multiply into the canonical softmax scale, while the output multiplier v_scale requires an exact provider argument binding.

Host injected-module protocol freezes the upstream signature, 32 MiB scratch metadata, output/LSE allocation, NHD/HND codes, argument order, and the upstream decode behavior that discards requested LSE. No JIT artifact is compiled or loaded.

Public wrapper covers packed/separate paged KV, graph lifecycle, scalar scales, output/LSE buffers, and multi-token causal decode. Host reference is explicit; an NPU workspace owns a private mode-bound provider resolver. An FP8 kv_data_type canonicalizes into a per-tensor QuantSpec. Separate bare FP8 K/V provider inputs use virtual scalar unit scales only under an exact omission declaration; combined provider storage remains fail-closed until a verified zero-copy slot-view binding exists.

Exact snapshot signature. Host reference reports (0, 0). Provider queries use an unpublished runtime fork over the wrapper's frozen registry and return the selected operation's caller-workspace requirement without mutating active plan state; package-managed workspace currently reports (0, 0).
For an NPU provider plan, an FP8 kv_data_type is normalized into the canonical per-tensor QuantSpec before selection; the Host oracle continues to read logical FP8 ReferenceTensor inputs directly.

For provider execution, q_scale/k_scale/v_scale remain independent dynamic scalar sources on the reusable plan. A provider accepting broader forms cannot widen the public decode contract. Unquantized packed/separate KV is metadata-validated against the planned layout, shape, page capacity, dtype, device and access policy. Quantized storage/scale/zero-point views are included in provider alignment and output/input alias validation. Caller-owned out/lse require exact mutable catalog arguments and validated buffer metadata. Bare separate FP8 K/V storage is canonicalized internally; implicit unit cache scales require exact provider authorization.
